items.title: countdown-competes-with-reading
items.claim: Image #2 presents strategy and control instructions alongside “STARTING IN 7,” without a visible option to defer the start.
items.reason: A new player is being asked to understand the controls while the screen communicates a deadline.
items.suggest: Keep the introduction open until the player selects Fight; reserve countdowns for an explicitly confirmed start.

items.title: stick-meanings-separated
items.claim: Image #3 places direction meanings in a separate strip above chevron-only stick sectors, while image #15 shows those sectors without the explanatory strip.
items.reason: The player must look elsewhere—or remember the mapping—to identify what each thumb direction means.
items.suggest: Put persistent action labels directly around the corresponding stick sectors, replacing the chevrons and reflowing the controls rather than shrinking the labels.

items.title: reference-name-mismatch
items.claim: The reference button reads “MOVES” in image #3, but its displayed reference sheet is titled “TECHNIQUES” in image #6.
items.reason: Different names for the same reference add avoidable terminology to an already unfamiliar control system.
items.suggest: Rename the button “Techniques” to match the sheet and the technique stick.

items.title: opening-example-missing
items.claim: Image #2 explains the input combination abstractly without a named example, whereas image #6 explicitly pairs Lunge Punch with centered stance and forward technique.
items.reason: One immediately usable move gives a beginner a clearer starting point than the combination rule alone.
items.suggest: Add “Try Lunge Punch: stance centered + technique forward” to the introduction, using the same labeled input notation as the reference sheet.

items.title: text-size-unverified
items.claim: The HUD names and stick captions in image #3 are visibly smaller than the settings labels in image #7, but these raster frames cannot establish their CSS font sizes.
items.reason: Visual comparison alone cannot verify compliance with the required 18 CSS px minimum.
items.suggest: Measure computed font sizes at 390×844 and desktop for HUD names, timer suffixes, stick captions, countdowns, and technique metadata; raise any below 18px and adjust layout instead of scaling text.
